intent: Build a URL shortener service that exposes core APIs for shortening and resolving URLs, records analytics on link usage, and includes unspecified reliability features.

functional_needs.statement: The service shortens URLs: a client submits a long URL and receives a short link that resolves back to the original URL (exact operations to be confirmed in Q-2).
The service exposes a set of core APIs for the URL shortener. The exact operations are not specified (see Q-2).
The service provides analytics on short-link usage, retrievable through the API. The data captured and exposed is not specified (see Q-3).

nfr_asks.text: Unspecified reliability features. Too vague to map to a catalog entry.

ambiguities.question: Which catalog capability does 'reliability features' refer to: per-client rate limiting on write endpoints (RL-BASIC), contract-based input validation with problem+json errors (SEC-INPUT), Prometheus request metrics at /metrics (OBS-METRICS), or none? Other reliability concerns, such as uptime, failover or durability guarantees, cannot be built or validated.
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Each option adds different externally visible behavior, such as 429 responses, 400 problem+json errors or a /metrics endpoint. Guessing would add an NFR the user did not clearly ask for.
ambiguities.recommended_default: none (no NFR is added until the user picks one or more catalog entries)

ambiguities.question: Which operations make up the 'core APIs'?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This defines the externally visible API surface and which operations the system must support.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Create a short link from a long URL, redirect from the short code to the original URL, and retrieve a short link's details
options: Create + redirect + get details + delete + list all links

ambiguities.question: What should 'analytics' capture and expose for each short link?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This determines what data is stored per redirect, including possibly personal data such as IP addresses. It also determines what the analytics API returns.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Total click count per short link, plus the timestamp of the last click, exposed via an API call for that link
options: Per-click events including client IP / geolocation

ambiguities.question: Can clients choose a custom alias for the short code, or are codes always system-generated?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This changes the create-request shape. It also adds a conflict case when an alias is already taken.
options: Optional custom alias, rejected if already taken

ambiguities.question: Do short links expire?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Expiration affects redirect behavior after a deadline and adds a field to stored link data.
options: Optional expiry time set at creation; expired links return not found/gone

ambiguities.question: If the same long URL is submitted twice, should the service return the existing short link or create a new one?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This affects create-endpoint responses and how analytics are split across links.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Create a new short link each time
options: Create a new short link each time
Return the existing short link for an identical long URL

ambiguities.question: Which redirect status should resolving a short link return?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: A permanent redirect (301) can be cached by browsers, so repeat clicks may not reach the service. That reduces the accuracy of click analytics.

ambiguities.question: Which long URLs are accepted when creating a short link?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This defines validation behavior and the error responses for rejected input.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Only absolute http and https URLs; anything else is rejected as invalid input

ambiguities.question: Are short links owned by individual users, or is the service anonymous, with anyone able to create, view and manage links?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Ownership changes who can see analytics or manage links. Authentication was not requested and is not in the catalog.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Anonymous: no user ownership or authentication
options: Links owned by users (would require authentication, which is not in the catalog)
